newsitem.title: UK: UK computer networker Akhter plans July float.
newsitem.headline: UK computer networker Akhter plans July float.

text.p: UK computer network specialist Akhter Group Plc said on Tuesday it was planning a July stock market flotation that will leave its founder and chief executive Humayun Mughal with a stake worth over 30 million stg.
The group said Mughal would retain a 60 percent stake in the company, which is expected to have a market capitalisation between 50 and 60 million stg. Dealings are predicted to start on July 3.

Akhter said it hoped to raise 20 million stg from the float, of which 10 million stg would be used as working capital for its existing operations. The balance of the proceeds would be returned to existing shareholders.
Mughal, an electronics graduate from Liverpool University, set up Akhter in 1979, initially as a distributor of imported computer products.
The Harlow-based group has since focused on niche markets and become a manufacturer, systems integrator and supplier of PC network and database technology to mainly public sector customers.
Akhter made pre-tax profits of around six million stg in the year ended March 31 1997 on turnover of 36.2 million stg.

The group's clients include the Ministry of Defence and other central government departments, which combined account for about 52 percent of turnover. Universities, colleges and schools account for 22 per cent of turnover with the health sector two percent.
